problems: Cliopatria's Western Qin shape from 414 to 438 contains the Wuwei belt (374 cells) that is the Later Liang 400 and Later Qin 410-413 shape and belongs to the Northern Liang from 411; the Western Qin and Northern Liang dossiers correct it, the Later Qin dossier (412 Hexi event, confidence 1) and the Later Liang and Tuyuhun dossiers may need to follow.
Cliopatria's four Northern Liang shapes are one static outline that never includes Guzang (Wuwei); the Western Liang shape lies wholly inside it.
End years disagree: Northern Liang 439 (page text) or 442 (infobox capitals); the Northern Wei dossier gains the western Hexi in 441 (confidence 1). One year should be agreed by the reviewer.
Later Qin dossier dates the Hexi hand-over to Southern Liang in 412 (confidence 1); the Southern Liang page gives 406.

Missing counterparts in other dossiers: Western Jin has no 399 loss of Qing Province to Southern Yan; Northern Wei has no 399 gain of Huatai from Southern Yan and no vassal event for Northern Liang after 431; Former Qin has no 386 loss of Zhangzi to Western Yan.

Wikidata Q4186404 is shared by two different states (Western Liang 400-421 and Later Western Liang 555-587); this dossier is Li Gao's state only, and Cliopatria's Wikipedia field for Southern Liang is 'Liang dynasty' (a different state), replaced by 'Southern Liang (Sixteen Kingdoms)'.

WebFetch returns model-written extracts, not page text: quotation marks in the dossiers are limited to phrases the extract gave in quotes, everything else is paraphrase; no infobox gave an area, so no factor-of-two check was possible.
